abstract: This paper proposes a temperature reduction method using model predictive control with space vector modulation in SiC inverter-fed motor drive systems. Conventional approaches to temperature reduction using MPC often face limitations due to the tradeoff between temperature and power quality. The proposed temperature reduction method using MPC with space vector modulation (MPC-SVM) generates virtual voltage vectors to obtain high current quality. Furthermore, the long calculation time to calculate the cost function limits the practical implementation of the scheme. The limitation of calculation time is mitigated by suppressing the calculation of the cost function related to unnecessary voltage vectors. This article achieves effective temperature reduction by minimizing cost functions for current control and reducing loss. Power loss is predicted by constructing an energy-based loss model derived from the dwelling time of voltage vectors. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified with simulation results.

Author Keywords: model predictive control with space vector modulation

articleTitle: Comparison of High Speed Synchronous Motor with PM and Switched Reluctance Motor Performances
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper deals with the comparison of High-Speed Synchronous Motor with PM (PMSM) and Switched Reluctance Motor (SRM) Performances. The design of both of them has been carried out on the base of electromagnetic, mechanical and thermal approaches. The analysis has been done for various speeds and loads. Finally, the results of torque ripple, average torque, losses, and efficiency are presented for different high speeds of PMSM and SRM.

articleTitle: Green Boat Monitoring for Sea Digitalization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The recent updates into the European guidelines 2023/2776 of 12th of October 2023 concerning the greenhouse effect's emissions monitoring of maritime transportation sector set the requirement of every ship docking into the port UE ports to be fully monitored according to emissions issue. In order to accomplish to this task is mandatory that ships/ports develop proper monitoring systems to be conscious in real time of actual emissions situation. This work suggests a characteristic monitoring system applied to a green boat that by means of proper sensors, manages to accomplish several monitoring tasks. All recorded data will be available in real time by means of a Cloud architecture accessible from every point in the globe. The Cloud architecture refers to the design and structure of the software, hardware, networking, and storage components that enable Cloud Computing services along with the new challenging at the Edge services. This architecture allows for scalability, flexibility, and on-demand access to computing resources, making it suitable for various applications and workloads like in monitoring for sea digitalization. The gathered data will be useful for further onshore in Cloud post-processing activities in order to check possible ship's emissions violations into the ports or for additional studies for improving the awareness of a certain area in order to reach the goal of sea digitalization. Future challenges may exploit the monitoring boat experience for making an autonomous process of harvesting data without the requirement of an onboard pilot.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Modeling of Commercial Off-the-Shelf Photovoltaic Inverters Using Neuromancer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: With the high penetration of renewable energy sources into the grid, using inverters with advanced grid support functions has become essential to maintain power quality and reliability. However, it is necessary to have accurate and computationally tractable models of the inverter system to assess the dynamics. Detailed models have been shown to be computationally intractable and require sensitive information from manufacturers to be accurate. Thus, methods that rely on data collection of the inverter system dynamics to analyze the main dynamic behavior of systems under various operating conditions and disturbances are important. In addition, some data-driven models might not be able to achieve high accuracy to assess system dynamics. This paper models a photovoltaic inverter based on the data collected while perturbing the voltage at the point of common coupling and observing the corresponding output current injected into the grid. The model is trained using the PyTorch-based library Neuromancer. A different dataset is used to assess model accuracy and computational time under different Volt-Var support modes. The normalized root mean square error (NRMSE) for each Volt-Var support mode was calculated and compared with other data-driven models in terms of accuracy and computational time. Using the Neuromancer library led to higher accuracy; however, it increased the computational time

articleTitle: Feasibility Study for Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer in Simulation with Big Data Focusing on Battery Capacity Requirement of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer (DWPT) has been proposed to solve the problems of electric vehicles. The requirements of DWPT are changed by not only the specifications of vehicles, but also the driving style of each driver. This paper presents the battery capacity requirements of DWPT by analyzing big data obtained from customers' vehicles. The proposed analysis method shows 99 % of vehicles can drive infinitely if they have at least 7.88 kWh battery when the output of the in-motion charging is set to Pin, WPT = 40 kW.

articleTitle: Preliminary EER Analysis for Sizing HVAC Rooftop Units
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: In daily life, a lot of time is spent inside the confined environments, for example: children in school spend between 6 and 8 hours a day, in the work environment 8 hours a day, in restaurants a few hours, and finally the rest of the time is spent at home. The environment, given the hours spent within it, must provide quality and comfort to the occupants. Indoor environmental quality is referred to as “Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ)” and is defined as the set of environmental conditions within buildings that can affect the well-being, health, and productivity of the people residing in them.

articleTitle: Study of Torsional Sub-synchronous Interactions of Drive Systems with Hybrid Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Electrical drives for large capacity compressors in a liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant have been investigated. There are two topologies for such an electrical drive; load commutated inverters (LCIs) and voltage source inverters (VSIs). Due to commutation of the thyristors, LCIs produce current harmonics with variable frequencies, and their interharmonics are significant. Therefore, torsional interactions should strongly be concerned. On the other hand, the VSI systems have lower harmonics in voltage and current. In addition to its performance, this technology has become mature and reliable. For this reason, VSI technology is getting attractive to large capacity motor drives. There is a configuration in which an electrical drive with a voltage source converter is connected to a compressor driven by a gas turbine drive, and an operation mode that the electrical drive supplies power to the distribution system. The power is usually smaller than the rated capacity of the electrical drive; therefore, the voltage source converter can be designed with a smaller capacity and cooperate with a full-rated diode rectifier, which is called a hybrid converter, for power supply to the electrical drive. This paper shows sub-synchronous tortional interactions characteristics of the VSI with the hybrid-converter for variable speed drive system for LNG plant. This study shows that the SSTI is less concerned with the VSI-VSDS. Therefore, the system is suitable to apply large capacity drive application in LNG plants.

articleTitle: Developing Two RNN-Based Algorithms for Electricity Price Forecasting in Markets with High Penetration of Renewable Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Precisely predicting electricity prices can greatly benefit various participants in the energy market. This is a challenging endeavor due to the inherent volatility of electricity prices. Studies have shown that as renewable energy generation increases, electricity markets and prices tend to become more unpredictable. To tackle this problem effectively, different ML-based algorithms have been presented. This paper proposes two novel electricity price forecasting algorithms based on Recurrent Neural Networks-Long Short-Term Memory (RNN-LSTM) and Recurrent Neural Networks-Gated Recurrent Unit (RNN-GRU). Two algorithms perform well in terms of MAE and RMSE scores, indicating their suitability for electricity price forecasting tasks. These results align with similar research findings and highlight their effectiveness.

articleTitle: Modern Digital Twin for Validation and Generation of Datasets for Machine Tool Spindle Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The manufacturing industry requires new services to manage machine tools effectively. However, the lack of training data challenges the creation of accurate machine learning or optimization models. To address this issue, this paper proposes a framework based on a Digital Twin that simulates the phenomena of a machine tool spindle. This framework enables the generation of datasets for machine learning by incorporating disturbances, such as vibrations on bearings, from multiple perspectives. The proposed methodology has been validated through a confirmed case study of a machine tool a hardware-in-the-loop real-time simulator.

articleTitle: A Fast Technique for Lithium-Ion Diffusion Coefficient Determination in Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Batteries are complex non linear electrochemical systems. Given the foreseen demand for lithium ion batteries for next years, it is important to better comprehend the processes determining the transport phenomena happening inside, since they are related to performance as well as aging. Diffusion coefficients are usually estimated using time-consuming and expensive experiments. This paper presents the two main approaches for the derivation of the diffusion coefficients and presents a fast methodology to estimate the diffusion coefficient of lithium using only signal processing.

articleTitle: A Comparison between Digital- Twin Based Methodologies for Predictive Maintenance of Marine Diesel Engine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: An efficient operation of marine diesel engines, onboard ships, requires advanced monitoring and diagnostic techniques for early detection of faults and degradation in the propulsion or power generation system. This complex problem has been recently approached by digital-twin-based fault detection models. In this paper, we report on two methods for fault analysis on marine diesel engines exploiting (i) an Artificial Neural Network (ANN) combined with machine learning tools and (ii) a digital twin simulation model combined with a parameter estimator tool. In both cases, a digital twin model of the engine has been used for the generation of synthetic data, but in different simulation environments. These methodologies are applied to two distinct case studies, and their outcomes are discussed, focusing on the pros and cons. A proposal for a method combining the benefits of both is presented.

articleTitle: Designing and Manufacturing a Solar Tracking of Photovoltaic (PV) Panels for Produce Maximum Power Electrical
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Using solar energy as the most available renewable energy can solve problems such as air pollution, drought and limited fossil energy resources in the future. Considering the low efficiency of solar cells, which are responsible for converting solar energy into electrical energy, the need to use sun tracking systems that increase efficiency is vital. In this paper, a tracking system has been designed and built that follows the sunlight throughout the day and always places the panel perpendicular to the sun's rays. In general, the control of sun tracking systems is done by two methods, open loop and closed loop. Also the open loop method is used using the location of the sun at every moment of the day. This system increases electricity production by more than 24.2% compared to fixed panels, which shows that the use of these systems can be justified.

articleTitle: The Effect of Short Duration Voltage Sags on LED Lamps
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: In recent years, the LED lighting market has witnessed a proliferation of various lamp models, characterized by diverse features and price points. This research delves into the performance evaluation of three distinct LED lamp models under transient conditions, aiming to shed light on their resilience and reliability in the face of electrical fluctuations. By rigorously assessing the performance of these LED lamp models, this study offers valuable insights into their suitability for diverse applications and environments. Furthermore, as demonstrated in the results, each lamp will exhibit varying degrees of susceptibility to different levels of Short Duration Voltage Sags, their duration, and their onset point.

articleTitle: Efficient Motor Drives for Wave Energy Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Marine wave energy remains a promising and substantial resource with applications that span large scale grid connected systems, to small self-contained systems that harness the consistent nature of waves to power remote sensors, communication devices, etc. Nevertheless, many open challenges related to efficiently capturing energy in wave energy converters (WECs) remain. This work describes recent wave-tank testing of a point absorber WEC that utilizes a programmable power electronic motor drive to study the impact of drive characteristics on conversion efficiency. Regular periodic wave tests reveal several parameters which can have a large impact on drive efficiency (control gains, dc bus voltage, switching frequency, etc.) From these tests, optimal parameters were also determined and evaluated in realistic irregular wave conditions modeled using JONSWAP wave spectra. The findings of this work may be of value to WEC power train designers and may serve as reference for further research on efficient drives for wave energy applications.

articleTitle: On the Improvements in Maritime Decarbonization by the Natural Gas-Electric Power System of a Ferry Operating in the Mediterranean Sea
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: the article proposes various methodologies aiming at reducing fuel consumption and emissions of a ro-ro pax ferry currently in service on the Genoa-Palermo route. Maintaining the actual 24-hour service total time (departure, navigation, maneuver, and stopover in the arrival port), a navigation speed reduction is proposed, compensated by the harbor stopover time reduction. The ship's original diesel-mechanical propulsion is replaced (through simulation) by a natural gas-electric system, which also produces on-board electricity, with the possibility of equipping the main thermal engines with specific energy recovery devices. This ensures further fuel consumption and pollutants reduction. In addition to fossil natural gas, biological and synthetic origins are also considered. The outcomes of the proposed solutions are commented from decarbonisation and economical perspectives.

articleTitle: Efficiency Optimization of Induction Motor by Automatic Voltage Regulator of Synchronous Generator Based on Search-based Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This article proposes a new method to optimize the efficiency of a 7.5 kW induction motor connected to a synchronous generator. The Synchronous generator is a part of an emergency power system supposed to provide power for the induction motor. In this proposed method, the efficiency of induction motor is optimized by the automatic voltage regulator of synchronous generator under different loads. The centerpiece of automatic voltage regulator is a DC/DC buck converter which feeds excitation winding. Due to improvement of induction motor efficiency, the cost of generation is significantly reduced. In the proposed method, a search-based method is utilized to adjust the output voltage of synchronous generator in order to find the maximum efficiency of induction motor. Furthermore, losses equations are presented which are applied in efficiency calculation. As a result of not using speed sensor, the motor equations are used to estimate the motor slip in each step of search method. Results of the proposed method is presented to verify the method performance using MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Predictive Branch Energy Controller for a Hybrid Modular Multilevel Converter in Quasi-Three-Level Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The hybrid modular multilevel converter was introduced in literature as an alternative topology for variable-frequency medium-voltage drives. The converter is designed to operate in a quasi-three-level operation mode. The focus of this paper is on a novel predictive branch energy controller which reduces the peak branch currents in comparison to the branch energy controller presented in the literature. This is experimentally validated by side-by-side measurements on a low-voltage prototype.

articleTitle: Extremum Seeking Control for Minimum Losses Tracking in Hybrid Excited Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper deals with the characterization and the online tracking of the minimum losses trajectory in hybrid excited permanent magnet motors. The extremum seeking control strategy is analyzed to ensure the convergence and the accuracy of the control technique. In electrical machines including a rotor winding producing a flux, Joule losses are produced in the rotor as well. Thus the optimal control trajectory to develop the maximum torque per losses has to consider not only the stator losses, but the rotor losses as well. This paper deals with the control strategy to be adopted in this case, with the focus on the hybrid excited rotor configuration.

articleTitle: Power System Stabilizer Redesign based upon Kalman Filter Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The paper deals with the robust design of power system stabilizers. The growth of renewables imposes continuous verification and tuning of power system stabilizer parameters to comply with a satisfactory damping factor for general system behavior. The paper initially presents the dynamic model of the generator, including the automatic voltage regulator and the power system stabilizer of type PSS2B. The synchronous generator model is of the fourth order, which allows, with a sufficient degree of approximation, considering the impact of the damper windings. The power system stabilizer is then used to estimate the network parameters by injecting a probing signal and measuring the corresponding changes in active and reactive generated power. The parameter estimation procedure employs the Kalman filter to infer the optimal estimated values. The results of a numerical application are reported to highlight the feasibility of the redesign procedure and the accuracy of the estimation procedure.

articleTitle: Position-Sensorless Control and End-Position Monitoring of a Two-Point Switching Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This publication addresses a non-model-based position-sensorless control approach for a single-coil rotating linear two-point switching actuator without permanent magnets. A shift current controller was combined with a position-sensorless signal-injection method, which enables reliable shift operations and continuous rest-position monitoring. A sinusoidal test signal is therefore superimposed on the voltage output of the shift current controller and the current response of the voltage test signal is obtained using a Gortzel-filter to evaluate the sensorless mover position. The position lookup-table(s) required for this can be configured automatically with initial measurements at the end positions of the switching actuator. The outstanding advantage of the proposed data-based control approach is that no system parameters need to be known a priori. The variable coil resistance can be identified with a dc current measurement. Moreover, a simple temperature and resistance change compensation method using the complex ac calculus is presented and verified in simulation. The performance of self-sensing end-position detection and monitoring was successfully evaluated on a dynamic test bench.

articleTitle: Extension of Low-Speed Self-Sensing Capability for Induction Machines by Using an FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Self-sensing control (SSC) of induction machines (IMs) down to zero stator frequency is still a challenge. In this context, a simple observer structure for rotor speed estimation is analysed with respect to its lower speed limit. Using methods enabled by oversampling with an FPGA, the extent to which the lower speed limit can be reduced is investigated. First, the non-linearity of the inverter is improved by using deadtime compensation (DTCO), which pre-calculates the currents at the switching instants and mitigates the interference voltage. Second, a grey box model (GM) filter is used to increase the signal-to-noise ratio of the current measurement. The GM filter is derived by using the difference between machine models with and without iron resistance. Finally, the two approaches are combined.

articleTitle: High Voltage High dV/dt Pulse Generator for Partial Discharge Testing with Adjustable Slew Rate
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper addresses the challenge of testing motor insulation under high voltage transients caused by modern wide band gap semiconductor switches. These transients can stress the motor insulation, potentially leading to partial discharges and premature failure. Accurate assessment requires realistic voltage pulse patterns, necessitating a versatile test bench capable of accommodating various devices under test, including entire electric motors and motor winding. This paper presents a standalone high voltage and high dV/dt pulse generator designed to meet the diverse testing requirements of motor insulation. The generator allows for the simulation of realistic voltage pulse patterns, adjustable dV/dt parameters, and high peak currents necessary for accurate testing. Moreover, it allows lifetime experiments to investigate the ageing effects of partial discharge on insulation interfaces, thereby aiding in the development of reliable motor insulation systems.

articleTitle: A Wireless Power Transfer Antenna and Active Rectifier System Compatible with Qi and AirFuel Standards
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-standard antenna configuration and active rectifier circuit for wireless power transfer (WPT), compatible with both AirFuel and Qi requirements. The proposed antenna configuration performance, considering the measured characteristics of available coils on the market, was evaluated by means of Cadence Virtuoso simulations and compared to the state-of-the-art, verifying its advantages. The proposed active rectifier circuit was designed in a 90-nm BCD process and enables reconfigurability depending on the operating frequency. A complete WPT system model, including a power transmitter (TX) and the proposed dual-standard antenna and active rectifier (AR) system, was simulated in Cadence Virtuoso for a wide range of conditions, deriving the efficiency breakdown of the overall system. In this way, a detailed performance evaluation of the proposed antenna configuration and active rectifier circuit was provided.

articleTitle: A Reduced-order Model for Simulation of Back-to-Back Start-Up of Synchronous Motors in Pumped Storage Hydropower Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper proposes a reduced-order model for the simulation of back-to-back start-up of synchronous motors in pumped storage hydropower plants aimed at calculating the starting time of the generator-motor set. It is assumed that the back-to-back start-up process is governed by a predefined gate set point-time profile to the governor of the synchronous generator. Simulation of detailed and reduced-order models are compared. Sensitivity analysis with respect to the parameters of the gate set point-time profile is presented.

articleTitle: Industry State-of-Art and Opportunities For The Use Of Drones In Smart Grids Inspections
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This work seeks to provide a clear and updated perspective on strategic drone technologies advancements currently available for power and energy industry experts. Addressed methods of drone use for given tasks include video inspection and fault mapping methods, autonomous drone inspection routes, and thermal imaging. As its main goal, the reader should expect to obtain a clear and straight to the point perspective of the current literature and industry state-of-art. Lastly, this work seeks to corroborate that the use of drones for power line inspections can be more efficient than the traditional methods, when performed correctly.

articleTitle: A Decentralized Fault-Tolerant Control Strategy for Multilevel CHB Inverters Based on a Multiband Hysteresis Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: In recent decades, multilevel inverters have become increasingly common in medium-voltage applications. Among the various topologies, the cascaded H-bridge (CHB) stands out as a particularly fault-tolerant configuration. Its modular structure, composed of multiple H-bridge inverters connected in series, allows for the implementation of a decentralized control strategy in which every H-bridge module is considered to act autonomously. In this paper, such decentralized control is described for the current control loop based on a multiband hysteresis controller, aiming at increasing the flexibility of the system and guaranteeing the fault-tolerant operation while inherently balancing the states of charge <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SoC})$</tex> of the power sources without further communication. Simulations have been carried out to validate the proposed method and identify its limitations. A hardware implementation is used to demonstrate the load balancing between the modules under non-ideal conditions.

articleTitle: A Step-by-Step Multi-Stage Filter Design Method of an Active Three-Phase Three-Level Rectifier for Aircraft Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The design of passive filters for rectifier topologies in modern aircraft is complicated by the variable frequency power supply and stringent regulatory requirements. This paper introduces a straightforward design approach that bypasses complex optimization algorithms, aiming to enhance power density. The referred method is applied to develop a passive, multi-stage filter for a bidirectional three-phase, three-level rectifier system.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis of High Voltage Contactor Using Acoustic Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: In this study, the fault diagnosis method of contactor using acoustic data was verified. Acoustic monitoring method can monitor the target without contact, reducing the risk of electric shock that occurs during maintenance, and the negative impact of target equipment due to the sensor failure. Although there are some previous studies of acoustic monitoring on rotating machines, there is few on contactors. In this study 30kV contactor was used to obtain normal and simulated fault data. Fault diagnosis algorithm was developed and these data was used for verification. As a result, it was clarified that proposed method can diagnose faults of contactor with high accuracy from acoustic data.

articleTitle: The Influence of Solar Flux on the Grounding System and Correlation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This scientific paper presents a correlation analysis between the observed value of solar flux (measured solar flux) and grounding system resistivity. Parameters of soil resistivity, how its value varies and how factors like temperature, pressure, humidity, precipitation, snow cover and measured solar flux influence whole grounding system. The influence of solar flux was identified to leave hypotheses that may affect to grounding resistivity. Seasonal measurements were conducted using the 3-point method with ground resistivity tester type M416 in March, July, October and January each day during two-year period. The electrical characteristics of the grounding devices of electrical installations do not remain constant throughout the year, but change depending on seasonal changes in the resistivity of the upper layers of the earth. In this regard, the problem of the influence of soil, geological and climatic conditions on the electrical characteristics of electrical installations have been a classic problem for a long time, but has not yet been completely resolved.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis of a Multi-Three-Phase PM Motor in Nominal, Overload and Post-Fault Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Electric motors designed with double and triple three-phase winding are solutions to improve the fault tolerance of the electric motor drives requiring to continue to operate even under partial fault conditions. The stator winding is split into two winding subsets, each of them connected to standard three-phase inverter. In the event of a fault, one of the two subsets is simply disconnected and the machine can continue to operate at a reduced power or with some overload of the remaining winding subset. This paper deals with a thermal analysis of a surface-mounted permanent magnet (SPM) motor under various operating conditions, designed for the rotors of a helicopter tail. The behaviour of motor is investigated when all the coils are supplied (healthy condition) and when only a portion of the machine winding is supplied, so as to verify which is the thermal limit for such operating conditions.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability of Type 4 Wind Generators as Affected by the Bandwidth of Current and PLL Controllers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper investigates the small-signal stability of type 4 wind generators as affected by the bandwidth of current and phase-locked loop (PLL) controllers. Using eigenvalue and participation factor analysis, this paper shows that high frequency dynamics may become unstable if the bandwidth of the current controllers of the power electronic converters is high. It has also been found that the bandwidth of the PLL control should be a small fraction of the bandwidth of the current controllers.

articleTitle: Stochastic Stability Assessment of Grid Connected DFIG System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper assesses the dynamic performance of grid-connected Doubly Fed Induction Generators (DFIGs) under stochastic wind speed. The detailed full-order dynamic model of the DFIG is exploited. The wind speed is modelled by a stochastic differential equation (SDE). A stochastic-calculus-based approach, which avoids the use of tedious time domain simulations, is used to determine the statistical variance of the DFIG variables for the stochastic variations of wind speed. The results are validated using time-domain simulations and the modal analysis for the grid-connected DFIG system. Moreover, the impact of system parameters (such as the controller gains and grid impedance) on the steady-state variance of the DFIG variables is also assessed.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Influences of the bandwidths in Hysteresis current controller on single phase inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: At the present time, due to climate change and global warming, reducing the energy consumption of electrical drives is a necessity. According to the advanced technological improvement of power electronics devices, the hysteresis current control techniques (HCC) has been widely used for small systems because of their simple implementation and excellent dynamic performance. Moreover, owing to their simplicity, insensitivity to load parameters' variations, fast dynamic response and inherent maximum current limiting characteristics, hysteresis current control is a rather popular one among different current control techniques. This paper investigates the influence of the hysteresis bandwidth of a two-level single-band controller with predefined target current amplitude and DC-voltage on the total dissipated energy and the current's THD of a single-phase system. The simulation model of the simple passive inductive-resistive network and the power inverter with the idealized switches (here: SiC MOSFETs) have been implemented in Scilab 6.0.2 simulation environment. The obtained results suggest not to use only a narrow hysteresis bandwidth but also lower current amplitudes and lower DC voltages depending on the application.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of an Optimal Control Strategy for Zero-Emission Operations of Shipboard Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This work introduces an efficient power management approach for shipboard microgrids that integrates diesel generators, a fuel cell, and battery energy storage system. This strategy addresses both unit commitment and power dispatch, considering the zero-emission capability of the ship, as well as optimizing the ship's speed. The optimization is done through mixed integer linear programming with the objective of minimizing the operational cost of all the power resources. Evaluations are conducted on a notional all-electric ship, with electrical load simulated using a Markov chain based on actual measurement data. The findings underscore the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in optimizing fuel consumption while ensuring protection against blackout occurrences.

articleTitle: General Control Scheme for Asymmetrical Machines Applied to a 15-Phase PM Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Asymmetrical multi-phase machines can be supplied by independent inverters thus further improving the fault tolerance referring to symmetrical windings. As the control of asymmetrical systems is more complex, this paper details a space vector modeling applicable to any phase number: it is based on the virtual equivalence between asymmetrical and symmetrical systems for which the opposite phases are connected in anti-series. The images by the connection function of the odd -order Fortescue (symmetrical) components define the modified Fortes-cue basis for the asymmetrical system. As these components are decoupling for the phase-to-phase magnetic coupling application, meaningful control strategies are derived with the possibility of implementing several rotating frames, thus facilitating the control (considering the specific harmonic mapping). A better insight of the machine behavior is obtained regarding the magnetomotive force spectrum, especially for multi star machine when some stars are switched off. These properties are illustrated with time step simulations of a 3×5-phase Surface-mounted PM machine.

articleTitle: Vectorial Control of a Multiphase Induction Machine for Electronic Pole Commutation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper investigates the multiphase induction machine ability to changes its magnetic field polarity by modi-fying the supply sequence, i.e. supplying different stator Park plane. Because the first space harmonic representation for a given sequence is not sufficient to predict the torque/speed characteristic, a multi-harmonic model is needed. This model enables to simulate the machine transient and steady state, and accurately predict the final rotor speed for an open loop trial, especially when the final speed is not governed by the main space harmonic (i.e. differs from the expected synchronous speed). The model is then integrated in an indirect flux orientation control, and allows to simulate the machine behaviour for any sequences on closed loop. For an experimental 9- phases squirrel cage induction machine, the time step simulation results are compared with experimental tests, and show that the flux control allows the machine to run at any speed, on all sequences. Moreover, changing polarity changes the maximum current level for a given mechanical speed and torque, which is very important for inverter design.

articleTitle: Dual Three-Phase PMSM Loss Determination Using Synthetic Loading
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Traditional approaches to determining losses in an electrical machine require mechanically coupled active braking. An alternative to the bulky and expensive test bench is synthetic loading (SL) method, which is particularly suitable for multiphase machines with an even number of three-phase winding sets. This paper presents the SL method for a dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous machine (PMSM) covering a wide operating range. The PMSM is fed by two inverters with a common DC link, supplying both three-phase sets in motoring and generating mode, respectively. Mechanical power is exchanged between the motoring and generating winding sets within the air gap. The measured difference between the input powers of the two winding sets corresponds to the machine losses. The main advantages of SL method are the elimination of mechanical coupling and the ability to conduct measurements in a steady state. The preliminary measurement results on traction PMSM with salient rotor across a wide operating range demonstrate the method's broader applicability.

articleTitle: Digital Twin Based Identification of Passive Parameters for PMSM-Based Generating Unit by an Extended Kalman Filter for Wind Off-Shore Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper proposes a digital twin model for the power conversion system for wind off-shore applications. The digital twin is used to identify the electrical parameters of the permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) and the three-phase boost rectifier. The digital twin model is based on the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) for online identification of the PMSG phase resistance and synchronous inductance, and the DC-link capacitance at the output of the boost rectifier. Hardware-in-the-loop tests have verified the effectiveness of the EKF digital twinning on the power conversion system.

articleTitle: An Analytical Approach to Design Energy-Efficient Propulsion Systems for Electric Vehicles with Consideration of Magnetic Saturation in Electric Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: With the impending bans on the sale of internal combustion engine passenger cars in leading industrialized nations, the electrification of passenger vehicles emerges as the sole viable option for automotive manufacturers. To bolster competitiveness in the future, it is imperative for automotive manufacturers to devise strategies for designing electric vehicles that are not only more comfortable, powerful, and cost-effective but also efficient, all within abbreviated development periods. This paper introduces a method for rapidly and systematically identifying energy-efficient drive motor solutions for electric propulsion systems during the initial stages of vehicle development. The proposed approach relies on analytical calculation methods, encompassing the analytical design process and analytical loss estimation. The analytical design process systematically generates diverse configurations within a short timeframe, while analytical loss estimation ensures the prompt identification of the most efficient solution from numerous design alternatives. To enhance the accuracy of loss estimation, the influence of magnetic saturation is considered, which can be analytically resolved based on a reluctance network approach.

articleTitle: A Reduced Switch Count, Self-Balanced, N-Level Inverter Based on a Dual T-Type Configuration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: A new Dual T-Type modular N-Level inverter topology is presented in this paper, featuring less power switches, gate drivers, and diodes, than inverters based on traditional multilevel topologies, such as Neutral Point Clamped, Flying Capacitor, T-Type and Cascaded H-Bridge. The proposed topology produces N level output and offers an intrinsic capability of capacitors voltage self-balancing thus eliminating the need of auxiliary sensors or voltage balancing algorithms, leading to a reduction of cost and power losses. A Nearest Level Modulation (NLM) technique is used to enhance flexibility and facilitate digital implementation, mostly in those applications where the converter's level count is high. In particular, such a goal is achieved by the NLM avoiding the use of a triangular carrier wave, because the switching states and the duty cycles for each phase of the converter is immediately calculated. Preliminary simulations have been performed to evaluate the performance of the proposed topology in terms of efficiency and power quality improvements.

articleTitle: Optimization of Hairpin Winding Schemes with Respect to the Common-Mode Current
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: With the increasing use of fast-switching power electronics, high-frequency behavior is becoming increasingly im-portant in electric power drive systems. This importance is raised further by the increasing use of hairpin windings in automated winding processes due to their high capacitive coupling to the stator core. As a result of the high frequencies, an undesirable parasitic common-mode current results. In the design process for a hairpin winding, this parasitic current can be reduced by using the shifting method. Furthermore, this method can be used for elaborating design rules for hairpin windings. Therefore, this paper deals with the influence of shifting the winding terminals on the common-mode current and the derivation of such design rules. To this end, the calculation method for the common-mode current is validated by a laboratory measurement on an existing stator sample. Lastly, the design rules are analyzed for their general validity, taking into account different voltage signals and winding schemes from the shiftina algorithm.

articleTitle: Stator Field Oriented Control of Cycloconverter Doubly Fed Induction Motor-Generator System for Plasma Fusion Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Experimental plasma fusion machines require large amounts of pulsed de power to produce strong magnetic fields for plasma confinement and shaping. The power system currently used for these machines is based on typical power-plant equipment: a motor-generator unit (MG) feeds a set of AC-DC rectifiers. The MG contains an induction motor and a synchronous generator, mounted on the same shaft. The MG operates like a mechanical flywheel: during charging, the motor accelerates and absorbs energy from the utility; during discharge, the energy stored is sent to the loads. For that, the output voltages of the generator are rectified and the resulting dc power is injected into the coils of the plasma machine. A doubly fed induction motor (DFIM) is used; this is equipped with 3-phase windings on both the stator and rotor; the rotor winding is accessible through slip rings. At startup, the rotor is connected to a rheostat (to reduce the starting current) and the motor accelerates to the steady-state sub-synchronous speed. To increase the energy stored in the rotating mass, a 3-phase cycloconverter (CCV) is then connected to the rotor circuit. The CCV injects additional energy into the system and the motor accelerates to supra-synchronous speed. The actual control algorithm used for supra-synchronous acceleration is based on the V/Hz principle and is implemented using the analog circuitry of the late 1970's. This paper presents a control approach that could be used to modernize this system - the method presented is based on stator field-oriented vector control. The paper discusses the control of a 12 pulse CCV that is a part of the system. Simulation results are shown.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control of a Dual Grid Forming Unit Connecting an Offshore Wind Farm and an E-STATCOM for Damping and Inertia Provision
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Future weak power grids pose significant challenges for the operation of grids interconnecting power converters. Recently developed dual grid-forming strategies for modular multilevel converters allow simultaneous ac grid voltage for-mation and dc voltage control. However, these strategies have limitations in providing damping and inertial power. Motivated by the grid-forming services requirements by transmission system operators, this work proposed the cooperative operation of a static synchronous compensator with energy storage in parallel with an HVDC connected offshore wind farm to provide the required inertia and damping power, forming a virtual power plant. The obtained system exhibits an enhanced performance and stability, obtaining frequency Nadir and Rate of Change of Frequency improvements of 65.8% and 76.2%, respectively. In addition, wind farm power intermittency is reduced, filtering out wind power variations over 0.25 Hz.

articleTitle: Air-Core PCB Motor Focusing on Electrical and Mechanical Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper proposes an innovative motor that aims to achieve ultra-high torque weight density, and the ultimate in mechanical and electrical integration. A new solution for high torque weight density is revealed by the air-core structure. A new path for mechanical and electrical integration is presented by three-phase PCB coils that employ multilayer heavy copper board. First, the construction of the magnetic circuit and its structural features are shown by electromagnetic field analysis. Then, its drive characteristics are also revealed by FE-simulation. In addition, the prototype of air-core PCB stator and its preliminary experimental results will be revealed.

articleTitle: Simulation of Battery/Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage System for More Electric Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The electrical power systems of next-generation commercial airline aircraft are undergoing significant development. Their main characteristic consists in the replacement of hydraulic, pneumatic and mechanical energy with electrical energy. The aircraft power system includes the power generation system, the distribution system and the loads. The More Electric Aircraft concept is a fast-developing tendency in the modern aircraft industry. This paper presents Battery/Supercapacitor Hybrid Energy Storage System for the More Electric Aircraft. This system is modeled and, on one hand, there is proposed a reasonable control strategy and on the other hand, the steady and transitory characteristics are analyzed being obtained a good accuracy. The achievements of the energy storage device are examined by simulation.

articleTitle: Part 2: Design Alternatives for Power Inductor of the 10 kW 3-Phase Vienna Rectifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The second part of 3-phase Vienna Rectifier Reference Design is focused to the design, comparison, and optimization of more various mechanical and electro-magnetic constructions of PFC/Boost chokes. On the market we can found a lot of final products which are focused manly for low and medium power (from 100 W up to few k W). But if we are designing a power supply with higher power (3 and more kW), a customized solution is needed from more reasons, as high-power level, mechanical construction of final products (specific dimensions), or the cooling method - cold plate solution or water cooled chassis is more complex as for air cooled power supplies.

articleTitle: Online System Identification Based Reconfigurable Embedded Real-Time Simulator for Electronic Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper discusses the Real-Time (RT) simulation of static power converters. It suggests an adaptive RT model that approximates the experimental power switch dynamics by transfer functions with varying coefficients. This approach allows matching closely the behavior of the physical converter, enhancing the accuracy and reliability of the simulation results. To do so, the RT model is associated with an online system identification process. This combination adds a layer of flexibility allowing for dynamic adjustments based on operational conditions, ultimately contributing to the effective implementation of digital twins for power converter. This paper presents the adopted online identification process and its digital implementation on a Field Programmable Gate Array System on Chip (FPGA-SoC) device. The obtained results are promising and lay a solid foundation for future work.

articleTitle: Behavioural Model for Fast Simulations of DC-DC Converters with Hybrid Digital Control Loops
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Originally, feedback control in power conversion systems was performed analogically. However, in the last decades more and more digital control solutions were proposed in order to overcome limitations and issues of analog control, specifically in terms of costs, integrability, reprogrammability and noise robustness. In particular, high resolution hybrid digital control architectures have been recently proposed, which allow to over-come the frequency limitations of basic digital control schemes. These modern control loops can be quite complex and a long time could be required to simulate them at transistor level. The aim of this paper is to propose a Matlab behavioural model of an hybrid digital control loop for DC-DC converter, which allows to study the overall closed-loop system with fast simulations and a high level of flexibility. In this way, the designer can rapidly evaluate closed-loop stability as well as the impact of Process, Voltage and Temperature variations (PVT) on the control loop.

articleTitle: PV-BESS CHB Operating in the Overmodulation Region
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: In this paper a photovoltaic (PV) battery energy storage system (BESS) cascaded H-Bridge (CHB) inverter able to operate in the overmodulation region is proposed. The overmodulation issue is addressed by means of a hardware solution consisting of an additional power cell in the cascade fed by a battery instead of a PV Generator (PVG). The effect of the additional BESS cell is an improved MPPT efficiency obtained thanks to a more quickly reduction of the modulation index when a predefined upper limit is exceeded. Numerical simulations carried out in PLECS environment evidence the effectiveness of the proposed hardware solution along with the control and modulation approach in terms of extended operating range and MPPT efficiency.

articleTitle: Study of a MMC-Based Three Phase Rectifier for a Back-to-Back Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The increasing use of decentralized of electrical smart grid and smaller means of production that are more sensitive to load variations makes the use of power conditioning mandatory. Indeed, power quality becomes a critical feature when it comes to these kinds of networks. To do so, MMC converters, thanks to their high flexibility are in the spotlight to help protect distribution grids. This article presents an MMC-based three phase rectifier that can be used as an interface to connect distribution grids to DC loads.

articleTitle: Recycling the Driving Force of a Hybrid Electric Bicycle in the Drive Cycle in Order to Provide Energy in Negative Slopes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper presents the design of the outer rotor BLDC motor for use in the electric hybrid bicycle, for this purpose, the electrical and magnetic design of the motor is done according to the nominal values and the outputs of this motor such as torque, torque curve according to speed, cogging torque, flux density, etc. have been calculated using the finite element method and the accuracy of the design has been evaluated. Also, the optimization of the engine using the Taguchi method with the aim of reducing the simulated cogging torque and the engine starting circuit has been designed using the pulse width modulation method to control the speed of the engine, which has optimal results in the simulation and management of the energy recovery cycle in the slope. The negative direction of converting mechanical energy into electrical energy in the generator mode in order to charge the battery in the control system shows the correctness and optimality of this research.

articleTitle: Stabilization of Passive Self-Bearing Motor Through D-axis Current Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Passive thrust self-bearing motor have been the subject of extensive research over the last few years, showing the possibility to reach the fully passive suspension of the rotor. However, this kind of machine becomes axially unstable above a certain rotation speed, requiring the introduction of an axial damping to be used on the full speed range. Recent researches have shown that when reluctant effects are present in such machines, it is possible to create an axial force through the D-axis current component. This open the way to introduce the required damping directly from the machine and not from an external system. This paper investigates this possibility by imposing, via vector control, a D-axis current component proportional to the axial velocity. It demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach through quasi-static analyses and dynamic simulations.

articleTitle: Development of Halbach Array for Fractional Electrical Machine with Bonded Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The magnetization of permanent magnets in electrical machines can improve performance, mainly if the Halbach array is used. This particular pattern is generally expensive and complicated to obtain. However, applying the NdFeB bonded magnets can provide a new solution for their versatility. In this context, the study of the Halbach array for the fractional motor has been conducted and compared with the radial magnetization. The first activity concerns designing the rotor geometry through finite element analysis. After that, the permanent magnet brushless motor has been equipped with prepared bonded magnets with the proposed Halbach array. The final comparison has been conducted through several experimental tests. The cogging torque, no-load voltage, iron losses, maximum torque, and efficiency have been examined to confirm the advantages of the proposed pattern.

articleTitle: Identification of a Lumped-Parameter-Model for a Dual-Motor Robotic Drive Train with Backlash and Electrical Preload
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: The mechanical interface of rotating robot joints require torque to speed ratios that are not suitable for an elec-tromagnetic direct drive. Typically, gearboxes are used to convert torque and speed, although these introduce non-linear backlash into the system. By using a dual-motor drive train, it is possible to electrically preload the gearbox and compensate for the backlash. In order to describe the system dynamics, a lumped-parameter-model is presented for which the parameters are determined to represent an experimental setup. Measurements are carried out in various coupling scenarios and the associated parameters of the subsystems of the models are identified. The measurement and the model are further adapted through optimization. Based on the evaluated transfer functions, the model is able to describe the basic behavior of the system. The measurements with coupled motors and activated preload indicate persistent differences from the actual system. However, the presented model may be applied in simulation and control to improve the dynamics of a dual-motor robot drive train with backlash-prone gearing and the possibility of electrical preload.

articleTitle: Primary-Side Dual-Control Architecture for Multi-Channel Simultaneous Wireless Information and Power Transfer Systems for Cobot Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper introduces a primary-side dual-control architecture designed for multi-channel simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) systems featuring a digital communication channel suited for a cobot application. Conventional multi-channel SWIPT control systems employ phase-shift approach and transmit the scaled output voltage through the digital channel, requiring precise signal reconstruction. In contrast, the transmitted signal of the proposed architecture is the output of the error amplifier, whose crucial feature lies in its temporal dynamics rather than its specific DC value, enhancing system robustness against transmission errors. The architecture was developed and validated through simulations conducted with SIMPLIS software. The simulation results demonstrate the better power efficiency of the proposed dual-control setup compared to the phase-shift configuration, especially under light-load conditions, where switching losses are magnified. Indeed, the dual-control method optimizes power switch performance by applying Zero-Voltage-Switching and Zero-Current-Switching, ensuring soft-switching and reducing switching losses.

articleTitle: Thermal Performance Of Cold Plate Cooling Of Sic Power Transistor In TO 247 Package
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This article deals with the thermal performance of the single silicon carbide MOSFET in the TO-247-4 package, mounted on the heat sink designed for natural convection. The article introduces the theory behind the heat dissipation of observed semiconductor structures. It describes the importance of thermal analysis in electronic design and provides the layout for the further development of future work. In the practical section of this article, the thermal analysis is realized by two methods, through the simulation in the simulation software, COMSOL Multiphysics and experimental measurement. Both methods are described and analyzed separately. At the end of the article, both methods are compared and resumed in the conclusion. The aim of this article is to show the reliability of advanced simulation software for the analysis of the thermal performance of a semiconductor device if the accurate model is created and the conditions are set appropriately.

articleTitle: Addressing Integration Challenges in Vehicle Roll and Pitch Estimation Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This study introduces a novel multioutput estimator that utilizes longitudinal and lateral accelerations to simultaneously estimate a vehicle's roll and pitch angles. Training data were obtained by performing laps around the Nürburgring track in both directions and a slalom maneuver using CarMaker software. Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise was applied to the accelerations to simulate real-world signals. Subsequently, the neural network was tested during a double lane change maneuver, with Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise added to the input signals. A comparison between the neural network's estimations and those obtained through the integration of roll rate and pitch rate signals demonstrates the advantages of the neural network approach. By employing algebraic calculations instead of signal integration, the neural network provides consistent estimations over time. Evaluation using Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) confirm the accuracy of the developed estimator.

articleTitle: A Harmonic-Based Triple Phase Shift Modulation Strategy for a Dual Active Bridge Converter in an All Electric Aircraft Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: A harmonic-based Triple-Phase Shift (TPS) modulation strategy for a 2.1kW, 270V Bidirectional DC-DC Dual Active Bridge (DAB) conditioning system for an All Electric Aircraft application is proposed in this paper. The DAB model has been obtained concerning the frequency domain, particularly resorting to the Fundamental Component Analysis (FCA). The TPS parameters are selected to both erase the flow-back current in the DC-link capacitor and minimize the voltage harmonic content on the load side. In this way, the reactive power minimization and the active power maximization associated with the first harmonic component are achieved. The co-simulation study of the proposed TPS shows a very good performances, also during step-load variations.

articleTitle: Weight Saving in Electric Vehicles Adopting LCC Compensation in Wireless Power Transfer Receivers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper addresses the weight reduction of electric vehicles (EVs), equipped with the receiver of a near-field wireless power transfer (WPT) system based on magnetic resonant coupling (MRC) to recharge the onboard battery. Weight reduction is very important to improve the performance of the vehicle, especially in the case of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). To this aim, the number of turns of the receiving coil made with copper wire needs to be minimized. It is made possible by the use of LCC compensation networks with appropriate values of the reactive parameters, which also allow a reduction of the magnetic field emission. The proposed method is presented, and several numerical tests are illustrated.

articleTitle: Transient Thermal Impedance Characterization of New High Power Press Pack Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Diodes are known as a critical component in power electronics and industrial applications due to their ability to handle high voltages and currents. To optimize their design for high-voltage and high current operations, it is important to ensure their reliability, especially with regard to thermal aspects. In this article, simulations were performed to investigate the thermal resistance and transient thermal impedance of a diode with blocking voltage of 2800 V and a diameter of 46 mm copper pole by electrothermal modeling. Thermal parameters such as resistance and capacitance are calculated and an electrical equivalent circuit, the Cauer thermal network, is developed in PSIM. Furthermore, the Cauer model is transformed into a Foster model. Curve fitting method is used to extract thermal parameters from the thermal impedance curves through non-linear regression in MATLAB®. Using the derived resistance and time constants in Foster network, average current of a device may be predicted at different pulse durations and shapes. Moreover, experimental measurements were carried out to validate the thermal resistance for the investigated diode. Finally, a comparison with analytical curve also confirms the effectiveness of the approach.

articleTitle: Robust Choice of Virtual Impedance for Virtual Synchronous Machines Accounting for Grid Impedance Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper demonstrates how the internal virtual impedance in virtual synchronous machines (VSM) can be chosen to ensure stability and robustness against grid impedance variations. Three VSM implementations are considered: a current controlled VSM with dynamic electrical model (CC DEM) VSM, a current controlled VSM with quasi stationary electrical model (CC QSEM) VSM, and a voltage controlled (VC) VSM with cascaded voltage and current control loops. Eigenvalues analysis is applied to demonstrate how the virtual impedance requirements for ensuring stability are different for the three studied VSM implementations. Moreover, it is shown how tuning of the virtual impedance can ensure stability for all three VSM implementations under all combinations of grid resistance and inductance in the interval rg ∊ (0, 0.2] p.u. and lg ∊ (0, 1] p.u. The results from the small signal analysis are validated using time domain simulations.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetic performance for conventional coil structures of Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Achieving proper magnetic performance is one of the important factors of coupling structure design for Electric Vehicle Charging in wireless power transfer systems. In this regard, the analysis of self-inductances and coupling coefficient between transmitter and receiver are essential tools. One of the ways to increase the coupling coefficient is obtained with the proper design of the coil structures. Therefore, this paper focuses on the coupling efficient variation in different conventional coil structures for charging electric vehicles under scenarios of magnetic structural changes. For this purpose, these structure coils with various configurations are comparatively studied to determine optimal solutions. Finally, the best arrangement design results in considerable electromagnetic behavior to improve the coupling stability under misalignment.

articleTitle: Yield and Hot-Spot Analysis for Replacing Bypass Diodes with PV Module-Integrated Microinverters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Photovoltaic modules with bypass diodes have been state of the art for years. In addition, optimizers or microinverters can be used as power electronics directly connected to the module to increase energy yield in certain installation scenarios. This paper addresses the replacement of bypass diodes with module-integrated power electronics while maintaining the protective function for the PV cells by means of a basic PV voltage measurement of a half cell photovoltaic module equipped with mono PERC cells in various irradiance and shading scenarios. A concluding comparison of the energy yield between a PV module with bypass diodes and the defined measures of the integrated hardware is presented.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of DC-Link Capacitor Size for Two and Three Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Two-phase open winding electrical machines have been proposed in the literature for their benefits in terms of peak torque and low noise emission. For this type of open-winding motors, a 4-leg power converter is required, allowing a power increase of 15% at the cost of one additional converter leg. This paper focuses on the impact of the two-phase open winding solution on the size of the DC-link capacitors, which is not covered in the literature. With reference to a state-of-the-art concentrated-winding 12slot/10pole 3ph PMSM drive, the DC-link RMS current stress and voltage ripple are comparatively analysed for different operating conditions. The simulations show that, under the same mechanical power conditions, the DC-link capacitor in the two-phase machine experiences lower voltage stress and similar RMS current compared to its three-phase counterpart. This effect impacts the cost, volume, and weight of the DC-link capacitor, partially compensating for the additional inverter leg required by the two-phase solution.

articleTitle: Investigation of Electrostatic Shieldings in Traction Motors to Mitigate Capacitive Bearing Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Electrostatic shieldings in electrical machines have the capability to mitigate harmful capacitive bearing currents. By employing Finite Element (FE)-simulations, the shieldings' effectiveness, influence on parasitic capacitances, and the associated eddy current losses are investigated. The study includes various shielding designs for both, the stator and end-winding part of a motor. Based on the knowledge gained by the Finite Element Analysis (FEA), motorettes with slot-shieldings and stators with overhang shieldings were built. Finally, the study presents the validation of the slot-shieldings' effectiveness by impedance measurements. The measurements confirm a reduction of the winding-rotor capacitance up to approx. 84 %. A large focus is given to the development of an appropriate design regarding its suitability in series production.

articleTitle: Enhancing PWM Rectifier Control through Kalman Filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: In this paper, different filtering solutions to enhance the performance of the PWM Rectifier voltage-oriented control are compared. The first strategy is based on a linear Kalman Filter, which allows for filtering the measured grid voltages. This, in turn, improves the accuracy of the phase angle and angular frequency of the grid, determined by the PLL algorithm or other methods. The second solution employs an Extended Kalman Filter to obtain the pulsation and filtered voltages, avoiding the adoption of the PLL. These two solutions are investigated in terms of dynamic behavior and computational burden. The investigation is carried out on a properly developed experimental setup.

articleTitle: Three-Phase Induction Motor Electrical Parameter Estimation Using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)

authors.preferredName: Victor Emanuel Correia de La Rosa

abstract: The three-phase induction motor is the machine most used in industry to transform electrical into mechanical energy due to its constructive robustness and simple maintenance. Knowledge of the parameters of the equivalent motor circuit can be essential for the size and design of drive control, increasing the efficiency and reliability of the system. However, these values are typically unavailable, which makes specific parameter estimation methods necessary. Techniques involving no-load and blocked rotor tests are the most common in the industry. However, these methods have the disadvantage of being laborious and time-consuming. With the evolution of data processing systems, computational techniques are increasingly commonly applied to this type of task. However, most of the proposed computational methods require specific adaptations for each machine, making the process costly and not guaranteeing convergence to feasible solutions. In this context, this work proposes a reliable and generalist method, based on artificial neural networks, to estimate the parameters of the equivalent electrical circuit of three-phase induction motors based on the data provided by the manufacturer. A total of 542 different motors were considered, with powers ranging from 0.75kW to 55kW. Two approaches are compared, the first using a single neural network to estimate all machine parameters and the second using an expert network to estimate each parameter. The results show that the expert system achieved the best results, reaching errors below 8%.

articleTitle: Optimal Sizing of Supercapacitor-Based Energy Storage for DC Rail Transit Systems Using an Analytic Hierarchy Process Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: Energy Storage Systems are widely recognised as highly effective solutions for enhancing the efficiency of electric Rail Transit Systems. Specifically, wayside solutions can significantly enhance network receptivity, thereby increasing the amount of Regenerative Braking Energy saved. However, determining the optimal size of storage devices is a complex task. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel sizing procedure based on a multi-objective optimisation framework. This framework formulates the problem as a constrained linear least squares problem, with nonlinear constraints linearised. The effectiveness of this approach is then evaluated through numerical analyses focusing on a typical scenario involving a DC rail metro system.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Current Sensing Technologies for Switching Current Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This paper deals with the comparison of different current sensing technologies that can be utilized in performing double pulse testing. Initially, the paper describes the principle of operation of the various current measurement technologies, underlying their pros and cons. Then, the considered solutions are experimentally compared through an extensive campaign of tests performed on a half-bridge power board equipped with SiC power MOSFETs. This analysis highlights the differences in switching loss estimation depending on the measurement technology used.

articleTitle: Interleaved Four Quadrant Converter-Based Active Traction Substation for Recuperating Regenerative Braking Energy in DC Railway Line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Symposium on Power Electronics, Electrical Drives, Automation and Motion (SPEEDAM)
abstract: This study addresses limitations in the Italian 3 kV DC railway system, proposing a bidirectional or reversible traction substation (TSS) configuration using interleaved four quadrant converters (4QC). Focusing on regenerative braking energy (RBE), the paper addresses the potential of bidirectional traction substations with interleaved 4QCs, allowing bidirectional power flow and promoting RBE revert to the main grid. The results coming from the case study highlights the limitations of the existing configuration and underscores the need for a transformative solution. This research models and simulates a new reversible substation design for the case study system using MATLAB/SIMULINK. Different load scenarios and system configurations are tested, comparing traditional and modern substation typologies.
